SOUTH KOREA STOCK MARKET SELLOFF: LEVERAGED ETF INVESTORS HIT HARD 📉

• 📉 South Korea's KOSPI index has fallen nearly 35%, triggering sharp losses for leveraged retail investors.

• ⚠️ The KODEX SK Hynix 2x Leveraged ETF has plunged over 80% from its June 23 peak, while the Samsung 2x Leveraged ETF is down nearly 75% from its June 3 peak.

• 💸 Many retail investors who used leverage and borrowed money to buy stocks have seen substantial wealth erosion, with some reportedly left in deep debt.

• 🏛️ South Korea's Finance Minister apologized after recent rule changes and the market rout resulted in heavy losses for retail investors.

📚 Learning for Retail Investors

• ❌ Avoid excessive leverage or investing with borrowed money.

• ⚖️ Leveraged ETFs amplify both gains and losses and are generally suited only for short-term trading.

• 🚫 Don't chase market frenzy or momentum without understanding the risks.

• 📈 Focus on disciplined investing, diversification and long-term wealth creation rather than high-risk leveraged bets.

What Jyothy Labs, Page Industries and Varun Beverages tell us about the moats we don't actually own? 

On 9 May 2026, the board of Jyothy Labs met and concluded there was no further reasonable certainty that Henkel would renew the Pril and Fa brand licences beyond 31 May.

On 21 May 2026, Varun Beverages signed a revised exclusive bottling and trademark licence with PepsiCo, pushing the term from April 2039 out to April 2049 and deleting the clause that had confined VBL to acting as a special purpose vehicle for PepsiCo's business

Twelve days. Same market. Same underlying legal structure a foreign brand owner, an Indian operating partner, a fixed-term licence with defined exit provisions.

This tells one thing about the risk that one should continously think through while reading this businesses? 

Will the outcome be something like what happened with Jyothy Labs or VBL. Let's understand this case studies and then the framework to think around such businesses..

ZERODHA CEO WARNS OF RISING MTF RISK AMID KOREA MARKET VOLATILITY ⚠️📉

• 💬 Zerodha CEO said the firm's ₹9,000 crore Margin Trading Facility (MTF) book is its biggest risk since the company started in 2010

• 📊 Around 50% of the MTF book is in non-F&O stocks, which can get locked in lower circuits during sharp market declines, making exits difficult

• 🇰🇷 Pointing to the recent Korean market volatility, he warned that rising markets increase leverage as collateral values rise, creating a self-reinforcing borrowing cycle

• 🔄 In a sharp correction, falling collateral values trigger margin calls and forced selling, while leveraged ETFs can amplify downside moves

• 📈 MTF has become popular only in the last 3–4 years, and India has not yet witnessed a COVID-like crash with today's elevated MTF exposure

• 🛡️ He added that SEBI's leverage regulations have helped prevent the worst excesses, but a sharp correction could still intensify selling in small- and mid-cap stocks

🟠 Impact: Cautious (Highlights systemic leverage risks in the market. While not an immediate concern, a sharp market correction could amplify volatility, especially in MTF-funded small and mid-cap stocks.)

reports.text:
AGI Infra Limited: FY32 Vision Is Built on Scale

📍Completed Projects
AGI Infra has already completed 10 projects with a saleable area of 95.19 lakh sq. ft.

📍Ongoing Projects
The next leg is even bigger.
It currently has 12 ongoing projects with a saleable area of 168.26 lakh sq. ft.
That means the ongoing portfolio alone is nearly 1.8x the completed base.

📍Upcoming Projects
On top of that, AGI Infra has 4 upcoming projects with a saleable area of 78.73 lakh sq. ft.

📍What this means for future scale
Completed base: 95.19 lakh sq. ft.
Ongoing + Upcoming pipeline: 246.99 lakh sq. ft.

So, the future pipeline is about 2.6x the size of the completed portfolio — which clearly shows the scale of growth the company is building toward.

📊 Other highlights
• 26 total projects
• 342.18 lakh sq. ft. total portfolio
• 164.25 acres land reserves
• FY26 Revenue: ₹352.54 crore
• FY26 EBITDA: ₹132.69 crore
• FY26 PAT: ₹94.86 crore
• ROE: 25%
• FY32 PAT margin vision: Around 25%

India Built a Phone Export Industry. Now It Needs Customers It Doesn't Have.

India's handset export scheme is aimed at a global market where roughly 61% of units sit outside Apple and Samsung and are served by Chinese brands using Chinese assemblers. The binding constraint is therefore anchor customer access, not incentive quantum or installed capacity, which is why the same policy tool that worked domestically may not repeat offshore. 

This is falsified if a non Apple Indian assembler announces a multi year export contract with a top ten global brand.
